description: Continuing the theme of truth and politics, we turn to consider the related question of what we should expect from politicians when it comes to lying. Some see lying as a black and white issue, but honest reflection of the nuance of public discussion yields tension between the desire for complete honesty and the reality of uncertainty, various media platforms, and the raw speed of information. organizer: NYC Philosophy and Psychology Readers Community
long_description:
Continuing the theme of truth and politics, we turn to consider the related question of what we should expect from politicians when it comes to lying. Some see lying as a black and white issue, but honest reflection of the nuance of public discussion yields tension between the desire for complete honesty and the reality of uncertainty, various media platforms, and the raw speed of information. That being said, there are different degrees of lying in politics and one suspects that there is some critical threshold which a democracy can tolerate. Join us as we discuss the wisdom of Hannah Arendt (1906-1975) who was a widely respected political philosopher of the twentieth century.

Participants should read the entire reading before attending this in person meeting. We will read the entire book for this week. I will be reading from this version [here](https://www.amazon.com/Lying-Politics-Library-America-Publication/dp/1598537318).

For questions please send me a message or post to meetup.

Best,

Brian

long_description:
Curious how to start learning something? Want to chat with someone of another discipline? Need a place to work on a project and share it with others? ISG is a social, game development focused work group that encourages people of all skill levels and disciplines to come together and collaborate for the benefit of all.

This is a great place to begin your game development journey and learn from fellow game creators as they work on their projects.

**Bring your laptop** and any software you will need to work on your game/art/music.

How it Works:

• Show up, introduce yourself, let everyone know what you hope to accomplish

• Ask for help with anything, get to know others, share your projects, or enjoy the company of others as you work!

• Share your highs and lows, high fives all around

***

How to find us:
It can be kind of hard to find us! We are on the 4th floor of the Armory building. Follow the signs to the restrooms, and nearby you'll find the stairs and the elevator. Take one of those to the fourth floor and look for the Seattle Indies banner.

***

Accessibility information:
There is paid street parking all around the neighborhood. There are paid parking garages at 516 Harrison St, 650 3rd Ave N, and at the corner of 5th Ave N and Harrison St. The Seattle Center has nearby bus stops serviced by the 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 13, 15, 17, 18, 19, 24, 32, 33, D Line, and the monorail. The venue is listed as wheelchair accessible. The Seattle Center has additional accessibility information available on their website here: http://www.seattlecenter.com/about/accessibility.aspx

If you are coming by Light Rail it is best to get off at Westlake Station and then ride the Monorail over to the Seattle Center which drops you off right at the Armory.

***

Seattle Indies strives to be an inclusive and welcoming community for everyone. By attending our events, you are agreeing to follow our code of conduct (https://www.seattleindies.org/code-of-conduct/).

## **Urban Reset La Dera Park: Walking Meditation & Movement**

**Hosted by Monique Marie \| The Free Spirit Yogi**

### **From "Doing" into "Being"**

In the heart of the city lies a pocket of peace. Join us at **Ladera Park** for an intimate, guided journey designed to help you shed the noise of the week and return to your center. This isn't just a yoga class; it’s a curated experience of stillness, nature, and community.

### **The Experience**

Our reset is divided into four intentional phases:

* **The Silent Walk (40 Minutes):** We begin at our meeting spot with a single chime of the singing bowl. You will receive a **Mindful Focus Card**—a tactile, hand-held guide to anchor your thoughts as you wander toward the oaks. Every few minutes, the chime will ring again, calling you to take one deep, conscious breath, notice exactly where you are, and continue your journey in silence.
* **The Movement (35 Minutes):** Once we reach the dappled shade of the oak grove, we transition from the internal journey to the physical. We will move through a grounding yoga flow designed to integrate the peace of your walk into your body.
* **The Integration (5 Minutes):** We conclude our journey by bringing the stillness of the park into the center of our being. As we settle into our final resting pose, the "doing" is officially done. This is your time to absorb the frequency of the trees, the rhythm of your breath, and the shift in your energy.
* The play. Lets challenge our balance by trying arm balances, inversions and new asanas to deepen our practice.
* The departure. One final collective breath to share gratitude.

### **What’s Provided**

To ensure you can remain fully "hands-free" and present, we provide:

* **Yoga Mat Backpacks:** To ensure you can fully immerse yourself in the walking meditation, we provide complimentary use of our Yoga Mat Backpacks for the duration of the experience.
* **Mindful Focus Cards:** Yours to use during the event.

long_description:
Join us for an uplifting evening of devotion and community at our Bhakti Kirtan, guided by the inspiring Subala Das! Immerse yourself in the soulful vibrations of mantra chanting, led by Subal and passionate kirtaniyas who bring the sacred sounds to life. Kirtan is a beautiful practice of call-and-response singing that opens the heart, uplifts the spirit, and connects us with the divine through the practice of bhakti.

Bhakti, a Sanskrit word meaning “devotion” or “love,” is the spiritual path of connecting with the divine through heartfelt surrender and loving service. It emphasizes cultivating a deep, personal relationship with the divine, often expressed through music, prayer, and acts of kindness. Bhakti transcends religious boundaries, welcoming everyone into its embrace of universal love.

This event is open to everyone, whether you’re new to kirtan or a seasoned practitioner. Come as you are and leave feeling nourished—body, mind, and soul. Bring your friends and family, and experience the joy of chanting and sharing a meal together in a warm and welcoming atmosphere!

**Pre-registration required**

**“Chant and Be Happy"**

Join us at the weekly Kirtan and in celebrating all current month's birthdays!

Welcome, please join our community for call and response Kirtan & Chai, chanting mantras and devotional songs.

Kirtan is immediately after the weekly SoundBath & Prana Lifeforce Healing (430pm-530pm). It is for everyone, participate or just enjoy the energy / rhythms.

Welcome to bring, but not required, a vegan/vegetarian dish to share for social after the Kirtan.

What is Kirtan:
Kirtan is the Yoga of Devotion (Bhakti Yoga). Derived from a Sanskrit root meaning to call, recite, praise, or glorify, put simply, kirtan is the act of praising and glorifying the Divine.

Why Kirtan:
Chanting Kirtan is a devotional practice that helps to uplift the mind, open the heart and bring inner peace. It is the fastest, easiest and most joyful way to achieve peace of mind. The mantras are mystical universal sounds that resonate with our chakras and remove negative energies. So, it is important that we chant so that we can benefit from this powerful healing energy.

long_description:
Title: What Is Progress? Knowledge Aggregation, Living Textbooks, and the Automation of Scientific Discovery
Date: June 20 2026 Noon - 14:00 EDT
Summary: Our collective knowledge infrastructure — the textbooks, professional training resources, and literature syntheses that define what professionals across disciplines believe to be true — is quietly accruing a structural liability. Compounded confirmation bias, stacked citation-by-citation into the foundations of formal knowledge, means that breakthroughs can take decades to reach the classrooms, clinical workflows, and decision-making frameworks where they matter most. Meanwhile, the deepest friction is rarely acknowledged: before any field can build meaningful consensus on "why" or "how" a phenomenon occurs, it must first establish honest, consolidated agreement on "what" has actually been observed. That prior step is routinely skipped, assumed, or fragmented across siloed literatures that never cross-pollinate.

This talk introduces a framework called "Knowledge Aggregation" — with two distinct but complementary ambitions. The first is descriptive transparency: algorithmically mapping what has been said, measured, and documented across a problem space, without imposing causal interpretation or narrative. The second traces the boundary between empirical observation and explanatory claim, building systems that can separate the "what" from the "why/how" — because consensus on mechanism cannot be meaningfully constructed until consensus on phenomenon is first established.

Both ambitions are now within reach. By composing tools already at our disposal — large language models, classical NLP pipelines, public data repositories, and engineering-grade automation frameworks — it becomes possible to model knowledge itself, rather than merely imitate individual experts. long_description:
# Bhakti Yoga Forest Retreat with Madhava Naidoo

[Hosted by Sri K. and Nitish B.](https://www.meetup.com/bhaktilounge/events/314941803/attendees/)

**Early Bird: $79 (first 12 spots)**
Join us for an intimate full-day immersion into **Bhakti Yoga, mantra meditation, kirtan, mindfulness, community, and inner renewal** in a beautiful redwood forest estate near Santa Cruz.
Hosted by Bhakti Lounge Bay Area, this special retreat features internationally loved kirtaneer Madhava Naidoo for a deeply uplifting and heart-opening day of sacred music, guided meditation, wisdom, joyful connection, and nourishing vegetarian meals.
Whether you are experienced in yoga, kirtan, meditation, or simply curious, this retreat is designed to be welcoming, grounding, and beginner-friendly.
Imagine a day where you can:

* Slow down and reconnect with yourself
* Experience mantra meditation and the Yoga of Sound Vibrations
* Sing, listen, and immerse yourself in meditative kirtan in an intimate setting
* Learn simple spiritual practices for daily life
* Enjoy nourishing vegetarian food and conscious community
* Spend time surrounded by the beauty and calm of redwoods near Santa Cruz Mountains

Retreat Highlights

* Guided meditation & breathwork (pranayama)
* Deep meditative kirtan + immersive live kirtan with Madhava
* Vegetarian lunch & supper in community
* Conscious cooking demo (Bhakti cooking)
* Karatal workshop + practical kirtan participation
* Vedic wisdom, stories, spiritual Q&A, and mindful nature connection
* Sacred time in a serene forest setting

What is Kirtan?
Kirtan is a joyful and meditative form of mantra music — a call-and-response musical meditation practiced for centuries in Bhakti Yoga traditions. No musical ability is needed. You can sing, listen, meditate, or simply absorb the experience.
Good to Know

* No prior experience required
* Beginner friendly
* Vegetarian meals included
* Limited to **30 participants only** for a personal, immersive retreat experience

**Weekend Retreat: Avalokiteshvara Meditation and Recitation Practice with Geshe Tenley**
[https://shantidevanyc.org/tenley-jun26/](https://shantidevanyc.org/tenley-jun26/)
**IN-PERSON & ONLINE**
Location: Shantideva Center 432 6th Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11215
Geshe Tenley will guide us in a meditation and mantra recitation practice, “The Inseparability of the Spiritual Master and Avalokiteshvara,” which was written by His Holiness the Dalai Lama at the request of his students when he was very young. This beautiful and inspiring practice is a wonderful way to create the causes for the long life of His Holiness and for peace on earth, while opening our hearts to compassion. It is also a wonderful opportunity to be guided by Geshe Tenley in deeper practice.
The weekend retreat and Friday teaching are open to anyone inspired by His Holiness and his teachings on how to become wiser and more compassionate. One does not need to have received any particular initiation to participate. The emphasis will be on the recitation of the *Om mani padme hum* mantra.

organizer: EvoLibri Groups & Classes for Neurodivergent Folks & Family
long_description:
Starting in Spring 2026, EvoLibri will offer a 10-week Dungeons & Dragons social skills program designed for older teens and young adults. In this program, participants learn the fundamentals of D&D while building vital skills in a structured, neurodivergent-affirming environment. This 10-week group integrates therapeutic approaches and research-supported benefits of tabletop roleplaying games, led by a practiced (and enthusiastic!) DM with licensed professional supervision. The weekly 2-hour course will be taught in closed cohorts with a ratio of no more than 6:1. Participants must attend one pre-class session/intake prior to group start.

***Skills covered include the following:***

* Develop Self-Concepts – use role play to safely explore who you can become
* Conflict Resolution – practice managing disagreement, frustration, and find paths to repair relationships with others
* Communication Skills – learn the elements of constructive dialogue and the ability to share needs and wants while engaging in team-building exercises
* Problem Solving – overcome difficult situations by working through challenges with peers
* Social Navigation – recognize social cues, boundaries, and expectations while navigating group dynamics

***Getting Started:***

* For Experienced D&D Players: schedule and complete your complimentary 30-minute intake session focused on character creation and group guidelines.
* For Beginners: attend a 2-hour introductory group session where we teach you everything you will need to know! No prior experience required!

**This class will take place in-person and via Zoom every Saturday from 1-3 PM from June 13 to August 15, 2026. Please apply through our [website](https://evolibri.com/series/dungeons-dragons-class-therapeutic-rpg-for-older-teens-and-adults-2/) or email programs@evolibri.com for registration info.**

* **Early Bird Registration Deadline: May 14, 2026**
* **Final Registration Deadline: June 6, 2026**

long_description:
Hey Poetry Lovers!

This group is on a roll. Here’s the gist:

We meet at the **Capital One Café in Chinatown** from **12pm - 2pm** every other week.

For enrichment, we start by reading and reflecting on a **“published poem”**, suggested by someone in the group. No advance preparation is necessary. But feel free to check out some of the poems we’ve read [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vSyE_wCLQCPHRrKmN5F9tOIeeRQUZESxjRXGVBoCF2uU8Gm0_d0uECiCBCQXEy6ksxfsBOhtRIOpW3T/pubhtml?gid=0&single=true&widget=true&headers=false%22%3E%3C/iframe%3E). Or submit suggestions for future meetings [here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSexGc2Z2Kp6bZW0D3_hfJ7NUUkfNHf7TXX-43FglCeBd9EF2Q/viewform?usp=send_form).

Next, we **share our work and offer feedback**. Depending on attendance, everyone gets \~10 minutes to use as they like. (No need to share, though; you’re welcome to come even if you prefer just to listen.)

We maintain a **Discord server** to help share our work and communicate outside our bi-weekly meet-ups. If you haven’t used Discord before, take a moment to download it and create an account before arriving. When we meet you on Saturday, we will add you to our server, the “DC Poetry Workshop”, and can help you navigate the app if you have questions.

Finally, if you plan on sharing a poem, consider how you will do so. Some options include:

* Print 5-10 copies to distribute in person
* Take and share screenshots in the Discord chat.
* Copy the poem into a google doc, change sharing settings to “anyone with link”, and copy the google doc link into the Discord chat.

Most importantly, we’re excited to meet you!

Catch you on Saturday,

Diego / Ian / Cayden / Nate / Otasha / Lia / An

long_description:
**ACA is a peer-support group for those people who are healing from the effects of being brought up in an alcoholic or dysfunctional household. This can include neglect, mental illness and outright abuse. A few family types have been identified here: https://adultchildren.org/newcomer-family-types/**

**We can meet in room 004 in the basement. Enter from the handicap ramp and take the stairs or elevator to the basement level. But if it gets stuffy in there we can also use the library that has an AC. We can decide in the moment.**

**Note that each week we will be reading from texts that fall outside the formally published texts from ACA.**

**The Power of the Meeting**

**At the heart of ACA is our commitment to meeting with one another. We understand that recovery cannot happen in isolation. By coming together, we:**

**1)Learn and grow using inspiring literature**
**2)Practice new behaviors leading to happier, more functional lives**
**3)Develop and hone essential relationship skills**
**4)Find safe environments to work through lifelong issues**
**5)Heal through connection with others who share similar experiences**

**If you are new to ACA you can find more information on the website at www.adultchildren.org**

Spring has finally sprung and it's the perfect time to meet, mix and mingle with other singles for a "Date Walk" at one of New York City’s hottest attractions – Little Island! Located at Pier 55 on Manhattan’s Hudson River Park, Little Island is a floating park full of greenery, open spaces, viewpoints, and more.
Our "Sunset Singles Strolls" are an extremely popular way to meet others in a safe, outdoor setting. Enjoy a fun way to meet others while getting fresh air and exercise. This event very casual and non-awkward + our host will help to make introductions.
During the walk, you will randomly be paired with other singles in the beginning then rotate at designated times so that you get to meet everyone participating. We'll make several stops along the park so that people can take pictures and admire the beautiful views.
We'll circle the island a couple of times and then afterwards, we'll continue the walk along the Hudson River. Once the walk is over, you're welcome to hang out and exchange contact info with others.
Experience all the components of the "island", nestled among flowers, trees and shrubs, along with dazzling views of other portions of Hudson River Park, New York City and the Hudson River. The landscape is diverse, with green lawns, small slopes, and winding walkways.

Socrates Cafés are gatherings around the world where people from different backgrounds get together and exchange thoughtful ideas and experiences while embracing the Socratic Method; the idea that we learn more when we question, and question with others.

long_description:
Socrates Cafés are gatherings around the world where people from different backgrounds get together and exchange thoughtful ideas and experiences while embracing the Socratic Method; the idea that we learn more when we question, and question with others.
Although this may be considered a "philosophical" group, there are no rules as to what is discussed. Those attending decide upon the questions of the night. Usually, the topics revolve around social concerns, moral issues, and the first principles of things.

Prior to each meeting we vote online for the questions we will discuss. That way, we will have enough time to ruminate on them and have more in-depth conversations. If you RSVP to a meeting, you may post your question in the event comments section below. I'll send out a survey for voting a few days prior to the meetup. We discuss two questions each night. So you will get to cast two votes in the survey.
When we meet, we break into smaller groups of five to seven to discuss the top two vote-getters. Each group discusses one question for around 45-50 minutes, and we then take a short break. After reconvening, each group moves on to its second question.

Hope to see you there!

-Brian

long_description:
**WHAT TO EXPECT**
Kirtan Soulfest is simply a transcendental party guaranteed to uplift you mentally, physically, and emotionally. The sacred mantras chanted in a call-and-response manner is the prescribed method given in the Vedas to link the inner divinity within all of us. This link connects us to the real happiness, peace and love we are all searching for.
Come with an open heart, dance and leave with an overflow of LOVE!

**WHAT IS MANTRA MEDITATION?**
Mantra Meditation is a type of Sound Bath and Yoga which is an immersive experience combining powerful soundwaves and group singing/chanting to help individuals better connect with their inner selves. Yoga means to unite, Mantra Meditation will help unite your mind to your body and soul.
The sounds and singing during a Mantra Meditation session are an invitation to journey into a deeper state of consciousness as an opportunity to gain perspective on what's going on within you. The goal of the experience is to invite deep relaxation, restoration and explore self-inquiry and self-discovery.

**WHO IS THIS FOR?**
Mantra Meditation is a growing movement in North America derived from ancient Vedic traditions and is applicable to everyone. However, some examples of individuals who might greatly benefit from Mantra Meditation are:

* If you want to relax, refresh and nourish yourself
* Stress, anxiety, or overwhelm dominate your life
* You're challenged by illness
* Grieving the loss of someone or even the past
* You're seeking a breakthrough in understanding your higher purpose
* You're looking to deepen your healing wisdom and spiritual connection
* You're wanting to connect with a community of compassionate, inclusive and supportive beings alike

Mantra meditation has different effects on everyone and is a deeply personal interaction with the sound vibrations.

long_description:
Experience the transformative power of Osho’s Dynamic Kundalinī Meditation, a moving meditation designed to awaken energy, release emotional tension, and bring the body and mind into a state of deep presence and aliveness. Blending breath, movement, shaking, dance, stillness, and awareness, this practice helps dissolve accumulated stress while opening space for spontaneity, freedom, and inner silence.
The meditation begins with vigorous shaking to loosen physical and energetic blockages, followed by free-form movement and dance that encourages authentic expression and liberation from mental control. As the energy rises and the body softens, the practice gradually transitions into stillness and silent witnessing — allowing participants to observe the mind with greater clarity and spaciousness.

Unlike traditional seated meditation alone, Osho’s active meditations recognize the restless and overstimulated nature of the modern mind, using movement and catharsis as gateways into deeper states of meditation and consciousness. This practice can be both energizing and deeply grounding, offering an opportunity to reconnect with the body, awaken dormant vitality, and experience meditation as a living, embodied process.

No prior meditation experience is necessary. Participants are encouraged to wear comfortable clothing, remain open to the experience, and fully immerse themselves in the journey.

long_description:
**Mysore Style Ashtanga Vinyasa Yoga**
Mysore Style Ashtanga Vinyasa Yoga is named after the city in South India; Mysore where this transformative practice originated from the co-founders Krishnamacharya & K. Pattabhi Jois nearly 90 years ago. Mysore style means you work at your own pace while the teacher provides tailored instruction from giving postures, asking questions, & giving hands-on adjustments when necessary. The beauty of Mysore is you don’t need to keep up with the teacher or other students in the room since it is an individual practice similar to an individual playing a song on a guitar, doing a dance or doing a kata in martial arts in a customized way. Since the same postures are repeated each time you can memorize the sequence giving you practice to take home with you or wherever you roam on Mother Earth.
Bio:
Shane has had daily Mysore yoga practice for nearly 20 years. He practiced and studied with/ Master teachers in North America & India including Richard Freeman, Mary Taylor, Rolf Naujokat, & Marci Naujokat. Shane has had a daily yoga practice since 2003 & has been teaching yoga since 2004.

long_description:
**About This Group**

Real Talk Christianity is an interactive, discussion-based gathering—not a lecture or formal church service. We make room for questions, struggles, and doubt that come from a genuine desire to seek God.

**Meeting Details**

Monday, 7–9 PM | South Bay Coffee Shop Location will be sent to you once you RSVP.

**What to Expect**

This is the first gathering of Real Talk Christianity, an emotionally honest Christian community for people struggling to reconcile deep faith with difficult lived experience.

We’re starting with Elijah—a Bible character who embodies both spiritual power and deep exhaustion. James 5:17 says, “Elijah was a man just like us.” He stood on Mount Carmel in fire and faith, then ran into the wilderness wanting to die (1 Kings 19). God didn’t scold him; He met him with rest, food, companionship, and a gentle voice.

**This night is for anyone who:**

* Feels spiritually weary, tested, or distant from God
* Is questioning, doubting, or confused but still seeking
* Wants honest, Christ-centered conversation without shame or performance
* Is curious about Christianity or newly exploring faith

**The Evening Flow**

7:00–7:20 PM — Settle In Optional snacks / shared meal, casual connection

7:20–7:30 PM — Opening Prayer Centering our time on God’s presence and guidance

7:30–7:40 PM — Optional Check-In Simple prompt: “What’s something you’re carrying into tonight?”  7:40–7:50 PM — Praise & Worship One contemporary song to shift the atmosphere and welcome the Holy Spirit

7:50–8:40 PM — Scripture & Real Talk: Elijah
  We’ll read 1 Kings 19:1–18 and James 5:17, then explore:
* Where do you see yourself in Elijah’s story (the high, the low, or both)?
* What do you need from God right now that Elijah received (rest, food, companionship, a gentle word)?

Participation is always voluntary. Some share deeply; others listen and reflect.

8:40–8:55 PM — Optional Prayer Requests & Closing Prayer  Leaving encouraged, not “fixed.”

I will facilitate these workshops with over 30 years of experience as a therapist, facilitator, and presenter in my repertoire.

I want to create a truly healing group experience that educates, encourages, and inspires everyone in the room.

We will explore types of love, intention, mindfulness, manifestation, Law of Attraction, self-love and self-care. You will gain new tools in your toolbox too as you Manifest True Love as time unfolds! We will explore our beliefs about relationships, true love, self-love, dating, sex, communication, and spirituality. Each participant still does their own work.

You have the opportunity to fall in love with yourself and explore the possibility of attracting a loving relationship that reflects that love.

The relationship you have with another and with yourself are themes to be discovered in this experiential and didactic therapeutic learning environment. The greatest path to learning as an adult is through experience, so as you participate in all of the workshops, you will glean more insight and skills as you manifest.

title: Navigating your content career in the age of AI
description:
Whether you’re a job-seeker or an established content pro thinking about what’s next in your career, it can be difficult to get a clear picture of the impact AI is having on content work. This panel will give you three unique perspectives on how people in different organizations are approaching AI, from the tools they are using day-to-day, to the AI-focused design work they’re doing, to ethical considerations and guardrails.

Join us for a panel discussion and networking. Pizza will be provided.
long_description:
Whether you’re a job-seeker or an established content pro thinking about what’s next in your career, it can be difficult to get a clear picture of the impact AI is having on content work. This panel will give you three unique perspectives on how people in different organizations are approaching AI, from the tools they are using day-to-day, to the AI-focused design work they’re doing, to ethical considerations and guardrails.

Join us for a panel discussion and networking. Pizza will be provided. **Space is limited to 100 attendees. We will need to register everyone with the building, so the RSVP cut-off will be at noon on Monday, June 22nd.**

About the panel:

* Mary Pritchard is a Senior Content Designer at Expedia Group who helps shape the Hotels.com brand experience and is passionate about exploring how AI tools shape our content design work.
* Katie Lower is a Sr. Staff Content Designer at Mozilla, working on the Firefox browser. She’s spent more than 20 years in content-focused roles and still gets jazzed about making the complex clear.
* Camila Pechous is a Senior Content Design leader who builds the systems, standards, and cross-functional practices that make great products ship at scale, drawing on a career spanning some of tech's most product-forward companies.

The panel will be moderated by Michael Metts, a Principal Content Designer at Expedia Group and the co-author of Writing is Designing.

long_description:
Join us for a warm and intimate evening of Italian culture, conversation, wine, food, and community at Via Carducci La Sorella in Chicago.
This is a small, cozy gathering designed to bring together people who love Italy, Italian culture, language, food, wine, travel, and meaningful social connections. Whether you speak fluent Italian, know a few words, or are simply curious about Italy, you are welcome.
Dr. Domenico Meschino will personally greet participants and help create a relaxed, friendly, and engaging atmosphere throughout the evening.
Your experience includes:
• Full Italian dinner
• Wine tasting featuring Stella Cometa Food & Spirits
• Italian food sampling and culinary discussion
• Italian conversation and cultural exchange
• Networking and meaningful social connections
• Stories, traditions, travel, and Italian lifestyle discussions
No Italian is required. Speak Italian as much or as little as you like. Listen, learn, participate, and enjoy the experience at your own comfort level.
With only 15 guests, this boutique experience offers a unique opportunity to meet new people, enjoy authentic hospitality, and spend an unforgettable evening celebrating the beauty of Italy.
Eat. Speak. Connect. Celebrate Italy.
Parliamo. Conviviamo. Beviamo. Viviamo.

long_description:
**Welcome to Bhakti Night** \- an evening dedicated to the wisdom and practice of *bhakti-yoga*.

The evening begins with a soul-stirring *kirtan*, a musical form of meditation, where the air will resonate with melodious chants and the rhythmic beats of traditional instruments. As the sweet sound vibrations fill the room, you'll find your heart opening up, and any stress or worries gently dissipate, replaced by a profound sense of peace and contentment. The *kirtan* is followed by a talk on teachings from the ancient yoga tradition which is always thought provoking and even entertaining!

As the night draws to a close, we'll conclude with a delightful vegetarian dinner. Savor the sanctified dishes, lovingly prepared with devotion, and experience how food can be an offering of love and nourishment for the soul.

Whether you are a seasoned practitioner or a curious newcomer, this program promises an evening filled with spiritual bliss and inner harmony. We look forward to sharing this wonderful journey of devotion with you!

**CLASS DESCRPTION:**
Join us for our weekly Indian dance class and step into the diverse, enchanting world of Indian dance and cinema. In this class, you will learn fun, feel-good choreographies to hit songs from Bollywood, and other regional film industries such as Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam.

The choreographies will be a lively blend of folk (Kuthu, Bhangra, Garba), western, and semi-classical dance styles, celebrating the rich variety of Indian movement and expression. One of the most beautiful aspects of Indian “filmy” dance is its ability to transcend boundaries, with no strict rules or restrictions, making it accessible and enjoyable for everyone.

Devi Sangha offers practical resources and insights for navigating both internal and external challenges. Feel free to bring a friend, and be excited to make new connections! 🤗

Through these ancient teachings of universal laws and principles, we will explore and draw inspiration to face everyday situations and fulfill our true potential. 🌺

If you’re seeking motivation, inspiration, mentorship, or simply a nourishing mid-week community refresh, welcome to join us. Bring your laptop. Bob handles the rest.

long_description:
We will read and respond to poetry in excruciating detail. It's fun, I promise!

We'll take turns picking a poem for us to read and respond to. Please come with at least one poem that you are ready to share—whether your own or one from another author. If you have nothing to share, feel free to listen in.

We will read each poem aloud, twice if time permits. If desired, the poem can be shared through [Proton Drive](https://drive.proton.me/urls/05PJ0BMSSW#es3lBdtVcr3y) to be shown on a laptop screen or viewed on smartphones. Paper copies can also be distributed, or feel free to just read your poem aloud---whatever you prefer works for us!

***Seattle Poetry Meetup is a proud founding member of the [Western Washington Poets Network](https://www.westernwashingtonpoetsnetwork.org/) \- check out their database of open mics and critique groups in the area\.***

VENUE

We'll be at the College Inn Pub in the U District. We've reserved the Snug Room—it's easy to find; ask at the bar for the Seattle Poetry Meetup and they should be able to point you in the right direction.

TRANSIT

The College Inn Pub is close to UW campus bus lines, light rail, and cycle routes:

* Link Light Rail 1-Line (U District Station)
* Bus: 44 from Ballard
* Bus: 45 from Golden Gardens Park, Green Lake
* Bus: 67 from Northgate, Roosevelt
* Bus: many other routes stop at U District Station a few blocks north; also the closer stop at 15th Ave NE & NE Campus Parkway.
* Cycling: Burke-Gilman Trail passes a few blocks south of the College Inn Pub; bike lanes on University Way and Brooklyn Ave provide protected passage north/south from the trail.

PARKING

There are various PayByPhone parking areas in the surrounding blocks, free after 8pm so you only need to pay for an hour. See also the College Inn's parking page: [https://www.collegeinnseattle.com/parking](https://www.collegeinnseattle.com/parking)

This session is **open to all** \- feel free to bring your friends\, family or anyone who may want to come with you\. The program will resume after a short break\, during which attendees will still have an opportunity to register\.

This program is offered through an Isha Yoga instructor trained by Sadhguru.

**Program Guidelines & Session information**
Sessions are on Thursday and Friday evenings for 3 1/4 hours and continue all day on Saturday and Sunday. Vegetarian lunch is provided on Saturday. Vegetarian breakfast & lunch on Sunday.

**Program Date and Timings:**
Thursday, June 25th, 6:00 PM - 9:15 PM
Friday, June 26th, 6:00 PM - 9:15 PM
Saturday, June 27th, 8:30 AM - 7:00 PM
Sunday, June 28th, 7:30 AM - 7:00 PM

Attendance to all sessions is mandatory.
No prerequisite or physical agility required.
Open to all ages 15 years and above.

long_description:
Re-BALANCE @ templ
A journey to self.

Join Templ & UNIONisCREATION™ for a deeply restorative evening designed to bring the body, mind, and nervous system back into alignment through the combined power of acupuncture, guided meditation, immersive sound healing, and intentional rest.

This two hour experience invites you to slow down, soften, and reconnect within the calming atmosphere of templ in Houston, Texas. The evening will begin with a welcome tea before transitioning into a guided inward journey designed to support deep relaxation and energetic balance.

As gentle acupuncture points are activated throughout the body, layers of sound from crystal singing bowls, meditative frequencies, chimes, and grounding instrumentation will guide you into a state of stillness, restoration, and renewal.

This experience is designed to help calm the mind, regulate the nervous system, release stress, and create space for clarity, presence, and inner balance.

Facilitators:
Dr. Sarah ~ templ Licensed Acupuncturist

Published originally in the Kannada language between 1990 and 2023, praised for their dry and gentle humour, these portraits of family and community tensions testify to Mushtaq’s years as a journalist and lawyer, in which she tirelessly championed women’s rights and protested all forms of caste and religiou
long_description:
**THE BOOK**
Heart Lamp: Selected Stories
In the twelve stories of Heart Lamp, Banu Mushtaq exquisitely captures the everyday lives of women and girls in Muslim communities in southern India. Published originally in the Kannada language between 1990 and 2023, praised for their dry and gentle humour, these portraits of family and community tensions testify to Mushtaq’s years as a journalist and lawyer, in which she tirelessly championed women’s rights and protested all forms of caste and religious oppression. Written in a style at once witty, vivid, colloquial, moving and excoriating, it’s in her characters – the sparky children, the audacious grandmothers, the buffoonish maulvis and thug brothers, the oft-hapless husbands, and the mothers above all, surviving their feelings at great cost – that Mushtaq emerges as an astonishing writer and observer of human nature, building disconcerting emotional heights out of a rich spoken style. Her opus has garnered both censure from conservative quarters as well India’s most prestigious literary awards; this is a collection sure to be read for years to come.

**THE AUTHOR**
Banu Mushtaq (ಬಾನು ಮುಷ್ತಾಕ್, born 1948) is an activist, lawyer and writer from the southern Indian state of Karnataka. She writes in the Kannada language and her works have also been published in Urdu, Hindi, Tamil, Malayalam and, most recently, English.

# 🎉 Boston Festival of Chariots (Ratha Yatra) – A Celebration of Joy, Culture & Spirituality!

Experience one of India's most beloved and vibrant cultural festivals—right here in Boston!
For centuries, the sacred Festival of Chariots (Ratha Yatra) has been celebrated in the holy city of Jagannath Puri, India, where hundreds of thousands gather to welcome Lord Jagannath, "The Lord of the Universe," along with His brother Baladeva and sister Subhadra. Amidst joyful chanting, colorful processions, music, and dancing, devotees pull magnificent chariots through the streets in a grand expression of love and devotion.
Now, this timeless festival comes to Boston!
Join us for a day filled with happiness, community, culture, and spiritual inspiration as we bring the ancient tradition of Ratha Yatra to the heart of the city.
✨ **Festival Highlights**
• Pull the beautifully decorated chariot of Lord Jagannath
• Experience joyful kirtan (live mantra music) and dancing
• Learn simple and powerful mantra meditation practices
• Meet friendly monks and spiritual practitioners at interactive Q&A booths
• Explore fascinating exhibits and cultural displays
• Browse spiritual books, gifts, and cultural artifacts
• Enjoy henna art and family-friendly activities for children
• Make meaningful connections and new friendships
• Savor a delicious **FREE vegetarian feast**
Lord Jagannath is celebrated not only as the Lord of the Universe but as the embodiment of divine love, compassion, and joy. This festival is an opportunity to step away from the pressures of daily life and immerse yourself in an atmosphere of celebration, positivity, and spiritual upliftment.
Whether you're seeking cultural enrichment, inner peace, family fun, or simply a unique experience, the Boston Festival of Chariots has something for everyone.
🌸 Come celebrate. Sing. Dance. Connect. Feast.

organizer: Hindi Poetry Open Mic — Bay Area
long_description:
This will be our 5th meeting of the Bay area Hindi Urdu poetry open Mic Mehfil.

Chaliye, shuru karte hain.
This is it, another evening for poetic minds to connect and celebrate poetery - Hindi Poetry Open Mic in the South Bay. We’re gathering at the Warm springs park Freemont for an evening of Hindi kavita under the trees.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/AFhfr3RKVzrNs6Nz8

Here’s how it works:
Show up by 5:30 PM. We’ll settle in, do quick intros, and kick off the open mic. Sign up on the spot if you’d like to share — you get 3-5 minutes to read original work, recite a classic, or share anything that moves you. Prefer to just listen? That’s equally welcome. Every mehfil needs its audience.

What to bring:
Yourself. Maybe a poem. Maybe just your ears. If you want to go the extra mile, bring a blanket to sit on and some chai in a thermos — we’re keeping this simple.

Who is this for?
Anyone who loves poetry — whether you write it, read it, or just feel it. If you grew up hearing kavita at home, if you scribble shayari in your Notes app, if you’ve been looking for your people — this is the space.

Logistics:
We’ll in the park, look for the group with the obvious poetry energy or call Shekhar at 9193389676. Free parking is available on surrounding streets. The park closes at 9 PM but we’ll wrap up by 7:30.

title: Jyeshtabhishekam Ceremony – HTGC
description: Annual Jyeshtabhishekam ceremony with Rudra Homam and Chandi Homam at the Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago. A significant ritual observance for Chicago's Hindu community.
long_description:
**Jyeshtabhishekam – Annual Sacred Ceremony**

The Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago (HTGC) invites devotees to the annual Jyeshtabhishekam ceremony, a deeply significant ritual observance in the Hindu calendar.

The ceremony includes:
- **Rudra Homam** – Sacred fire ritual invoking Lord Shiva
- **Chandi Homam** – Fire ritual honoring Goddess Chandi/Durga
- Abhishekam (sacred bathing) of the deities
- Vedic chanting by temple priests

This is one of the most important annual rituals at HTGC and draws devotees from across the greater Chicago area.

**Details:**
- Date: Sunday, June 28, 2026
- Location: Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago, 10915 Lemont Rd, Lemont, IL
- Admission: Free and open to all devotees

Prasad will be distributed after the ceremony.

long_description:
ISC invites you to hang out for drinks and casual conversation with other science fans. **Whether you work in science or are just interested in science discoveries and research, this is a *great* time to meet like-minded folks!**

At this Science Social, *WE* get to be the "lab rats!" Steve Franconeri, PhD, Northwestern University Professor of cognitive psychology, developed *[Point Taken](https://pointtaken.social/)*, a game easy to master at any age, that is designed to turn heated arguments into a joint exploration supported by mutual respect and honest thinking. He will explain his reasoning and the research behind it the game, then we will play it and provide feedback.

It's a great follow up to ISC's program last fall -- *Your Brain on Misinformation --* when Dr. Matthew Facciani presented his work for *Misguided: Where Misinformation Starts, How It Spreads, and What to Do About It.* Attendees were very interested in how to persuade relatives discussing politics and had a lively post-presentation conversation about how to have productive non-argumentative conversations. This game will be a great exercise in that effort but you certainly don't need to have gone to that event to attend this one.

**Monday, June 29, 2026**
**6:00pm - 9:00pm-ish (game presentation at 6:30)**
**[Half Sour](https://halfsourchicago.com/)**, 755 S Clark St., Chicago, IL ([map](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Half+Sour/@41.8725394,-87.6305898,18.24z/data=!4m6!3m5!1s0x880e2c970f9401cf:0xcadfde30a7663d8d!8m2!3d41.872448!4d-87.630322!16s%2Fg%2F11hbkts6fs?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDYwMy4xIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D)) at Polk St.

***See you there!!***

long_description:
Welcome!!

Meditation + Tea is a monthly gathering, for women of color to meditate and converse about cultivating more joy in our lives over a cup of delicious herbal tea.

This relaxed and informal gathering begins with a guided meditation designed to relieve stress, build community, and create space to unwind the narratives that block the flow of joy.
We will deepen the connection between mind, body, and heart through meditation, followed by conversation about living with meaningful joy over a cup of delicious herbal tea. (Our blends are cultivated and created by Ursula and Stephanie and shared for your enjoyment)

Our June gathering will be an evening of soulful movement meditation designed to help you reconnect with your body, breath, and inner rhythm.

Guided by a curated playlist featuring artists like Mariah the Scientist, Leon Thomas, Brent Faiyaz, Jazmine Sullivan, India Arie, Jill Scott, and other soulful R&B artists, we’ll move through an evening of slow flow, emotional presence, reflection, and release.

No dance experience is needed. This is not about performance or choreography, but about listening inward, moving intuitively, and allowing the body to guide the experience. We’ll close the evening with tea and reflective connection in community.

Come as you are. Move as you need. Leave feeling more rooted, softened, and alive.

$5 fee can be submitted via CashApp @ $meditationtea to secure your spot.

Space is limited.

Up to 60,000 runners line Peachtree Street on Independence Day morning for a 6.2-mile run from Lenox Square to Piedmont Park. The 2026 edition is extra special — it coincides with Atlanta's 250th anniversary and the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The race attracts everyone from Olympic medalists to costumed fun-runners, with massive crowds lining the route. Finish line festivities include live music, food vendors, and the famous Peachtree t-shirt.

long_description:
Hello friends! We're excited to host this summer outdoors, fingers crossed for a good, not-smokey day. We love this South Asian cookbook for its emphasis on local, family-run, sustainable agriculture and homey recipes from the same families.

**Official cookbook blurb:**
From Diaspora Co., the progressive spice company rooted in flavor and equity, comes a cookbook celebrating beautiful, simple, and seasonal cooking with 85 recipes adapted from India and Sri Lanka’s best family spice farms.
Diaspora Co. sources the most flavorful, fresh spices in the world from 150 regenerative farms across South Asia—from elders, indigenous communities, young changemakers, and brilliant multi-generational farming families across India and Sri Lanka who are leading the way in sustainable and climate change–resistant agriculture. Filled with culinary storytelling, *The Diaspora Co. Cookbook* highlights these farmers and their spices with profiles and evocative photography, plus 85 recipes for simple, seasonal, and powerfully delicious meals.

CEO and founder Sana Javeri Kadri and recipe writer Asha Loupy realized that eating with the people who grow our spices unveiled a whole new dimension in our cooking. For instance, the Mir family, who works all year to grow and harvest their saffron, shared not only their technique for blooming the vibrant spice and how to make sure every thread is fully utilized, but their unforgettably delicious dishes. Adapted for a global pantry, these recipes share the warmth of true South Asian home cooking at its truest and tastiest, starting with chutneys & pickles, snacks, and veggies, traveling through to mains from the sea and from the land, rice and breads, and ending with drinks and desserts.

title: Chai, Coffee & Conversation: Meet Fellow Desi Men
description:
Welcome to the first gathering of Desi Men’s Circle NJ!

Let’s meet, make new friends, and start building a supportive community for South Asian men in New Jersey.

Whether you’ve been in the U.S. for years or recently arrived, this is an opportunity to connect with others who may share similar experiences and challenges.

There is no formal agenda and no pressure to speak. Come as you are.

Topics may include:

* Making friends as adults
* Career and professional growth
* Immigration experience
long_description:
Welcome to the first gathering of Desi Men’s Circle NJ!

Let’s meet, make new friends, and start building a supportive community for South Asian men in New Jersey.

Whether you’ve been in the U.S. for years or recently arrived, this is an opportunity to connect with others who may share similar experiences and challenges.

There is no formal agenda and no pressure to speak. Come as you are.

Topics may include:

* Making friends as adults
* Career and professional growth
* Immigration experiences
* Family and cultural expectations
* Fitness and health
* Relationships
* Life in New Jersey

Our goal is simple: create genuine friendships and a strong sense of community.

All South Asian men and those who identify with South Asian culture are welcome.

* You are genuinely interested in a long-term, marriage-oriented relationship
* You have completed a college or university degree/diploma
* You are fluent in English and enjoy thoughtful, engaging conversation
* You have 2+ years of professional experience in your field
* You are passionate about career growth and personal development
* You have an ambitious, forward-thinking mindset
* You are socially confident and have had meaningful relationships in the past

long_description:
Within each of us lies a dream that carries us toward Africa. Whether it began in childhood or later in life, the image of the savanna, snow-capped mountains, and untamed wildlife stirs curiosity, emotion, and the desire for adventure. Kilimanjaro, the rooftop of the African continent, is the symbol of that call — a legendary mountain, a natural wonder that seems lifted from an African fairytale. With its imposing silhouette surrounded by tropical forests and arid savannas, Kilimanjaro offers a one-of-a-kind experience — a journey from equatorial jungle to a landscape resembling the polar tundra.

It's an ascent that leaves a mark not only physically but emotionally. As you climb, you don't just reach a summit — you rediscover a part of yourself. The peak offers a new horizon: clearer, broader, and more confident.

From a technical standpoint, Kilimanjaro is the most accessible peak of the famous Seven Summits and Seven Volcanoes. It doesn't require mountaineering skills and is successfully climbed each year by people of all ages — from 6 to 83 years old. The trails are well-maintained, logistics are excellent, and porters carry most of the gear, making the experience both comfortable and achievable.

For those who want to extend their African journey, the expedition can be followed by a spectacular safari in Tarangire and Ngorongoro — the land of great migrations, lions, and elephants, an unmatched natural spectacle.

This is more than just a vacation — it's a journey that leaves a deep mark on your soul and gently changes the way you see the world.

Highlights:
• Uhuru Peak (5,895m) – Roof of Africa
• Journey from tropical rainforest to arctic-alpine zone
• Machame Route – one of the most scenic paths
• Sunrise summit attempt under a star-filled sky
• Certificate of achievement upon completion
• Optional: Safari extension in Tarangire and Ngorongoro Crater

Celebrate the 22nd anniversary of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in the Detroit area, beautifully coinciding with India's Independence Day.

This grand celebration will feature:

- **2:00 PM** – Vedic Mahapuja (sacred fire ceremony)
- **2:00 – 5:00 PM** – Annakut Darshan (offering of hundreds of food items to the deities)
- **4:00 PM** – Patotsav Sabha (cultural assembly with addresses by visiting swamis)

The Patotsav marks the sacred anniversary of the mandir's murti pratishtha (consecration of the deities) and is one of the most auspicious events of the year.

**Details:**
- Date: Saturday, August 15, 2026
- Location: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Canton, MI
- Admission: Free and open to all

Special prasad and celebrations throughout the day. All families welcome.

title: Diwali Festival — Shiva Vishnu Temple Livermore
description: Grand Diwali celebration at Livermore's Shiva Vishnu Temple with Lakshmi Puja, fireworks, and community feast.
long_description: The Shiva Vishnu Temple's Diwali celebration is one of the Bay Area's most attended Hindu festivals. The day-long program includes Lakshmi Puja, special abhishekams, cultural performances, and a community feast. The temple grounds are illuminated with thousands of diyas and festive lighting. A must-attend for Bay Area families.
venue_info: 1232 Arrowhead Ave, Livermore. All-day event. Expect very large crowds — shuttle service often provided from overflow parking. Prasadam and festival food available.

title: Diwali Celebrations — Sri Venkateswara Temple, Pittsburgh
description: Diwali at America's oldest traditional Hindu temple with Lakshmi Puja and grand celebrations.
long_description: Celebrate Diwali at the historic Sri Venkateswara Temple in Penn Hills — the first traditional Hindu temple in America. Special Lakshmi Puja, Sahasranama archana, cultural performances, and fireworks make this one of Pittsburgh's most significant Hindu celebrations.
venue_info: 1230 S McCully Dr, Penn Hills, PA 15235. All-day event. Free parking. Prasadam and festival food.

title: Diwali Celebrations — Hindu Temple of Seattle
venue_name: Hindu Temple & Cultural Center of Seattle
description: Seattle's grand Diwali celebration at the Hindu Temple in Bothell with Lakshmi Puja and cultural programs.
organizer: Hindu Temple & Cultural Center of Seattle
long_description: Celebrate Diwali at the Hindu Temple of Seattle with traditional Lakshmi Puja, cultural performances, children's programs, and festive decorations. The temple community comes together for this joyous festival of lights. Prasadam and festival food served throughout the day.
venue_info: 3818 212th St SE, Bothell, WA 98021. Free parking. All-day event. Prasadam served.

title: Diwali Celebrations — BAPS Mandir, Los Angeles
description: Grand Diwali at BAPS Los Angeles with traditional pujas, cultural performances, and fireworks.
long_description: Celebrate Diwali at the stunning BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Chino Hills. The temple's pink sandstone and white marble architecture shines brilliantly when illuminated for Diwali. Programs include Lakshmi Puja, Chopda Puja for business owners, cultural shows, and spectacular fireworks. One of LA's most attended Hindu celebrations.
venue_info: 15100 Fairfield Ranch Rd, Chino Hills, CA 91709. Free parking. Open 9 AM–7:30 PM. Prasadam served.

title: Diwali Celebrations — Sri Lakshmi Temple, Boston Area
description: Grand Diwali at the Boston area's Sri Lakshmi Temple with Lakshmi Puja and cultural programs.
long_description: Celebrate Diwali at the Sri Lakshmi Temple in Ashland with special Lakshmi Puja, cultural performances, and a community feast. The temple is beautifully decorated with diyas and festive lighting for New England's largest Hindu Diwali celebration.
venue_info: 117 Waverly St, Ashland, MA 01721. All-day event. Ample parking. Prasadam and festival food.

title: Diwali Celebrations — Sri Meenakshi Temple, Houston
description: Houston's beloved Sri Meenakshi Temple celebrates Diwali with Lakshmi Puja, fireworks, and community feast.
long_description: Sri Meenakshi Temple in Pearland hosts Houston's premier temple Diwali celebration. The grand evening features elaborate Lakshmi Puja, thousands of diyas, cultural programs, a fireworks display, and community dinner. The temple's impressive Dravidian architecture provides a stunning backdrop for the Festival of Lights.
venue_info: 17130 McLean Rd, Pearland, TX. Free parking. Large grounds accommodate thousands of visitors.

title: Diwali Festival — DFW Hindu Temple, Irving
description: Grand Diwali celebration at the DFW Hindu Temple with Lakshmi Puja, fireworks, and cultural programs.
long_description: The DFW Hindu Temple's Diwali is the Dallas area's biggest Hindu celebration. Features Lakshmi Puja, cultural performances, children's programs, food stalls, and an evening fireworks display. Thousands of families gather for this annual festival of lights.
venue_info: 1605 N Britain Rd, Irving, TX 75061. All-day event. Shuttle from overflow parking on busy days.

title: Diwali Festival — Malibu Hindu Temple
description: Diwali at the iconic Malibu Hindu Temple with Lakshmi Puja, fireworks, and panoramic mountain views.
organizer: Hindu Temple Society of Southern California
long_description: Celebrate Diwali at one of Southern California's most scenic temples. The Malibu Hindu Temple's Diwali program features Lakshmi Puja, special abhishekams, cultural performances, and the spectacular sight of diyas lit against the Santa Monica Mountains backdrop. A unique and unforgettable Diwali experience in the LA area.
venue_info: 1600 Las Virgenes Canyon Rd, Calabasas. All-day event. Parking fills up fast — arrive early. Prasadam available.

title: Diwali Celebrations — BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Milpitas
description: Grand Diwali celebration at the BAPS Mandir with lighting ceremony, cultural program, and community feast.
long_description: BAPS Milpitas hosts its spectacular Diwali celebration, the Festival of Lights. The evening features thousands of diyas illuminating the mandir, a cultural program with devotional performances, fireworks, and a community dinner. One of the most visually stunning Diwali celebrations in the Bay Area.
venue_info: BAPS Mandir, Milpitas. Large parking facility. Expect heavy crowds — arrive early. Modest dress code required inside the mandir.

title: Diwali Mela — BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir Houston
description: Grand Diwali Mela at BAPS Houston with lighting ceremony, rangoli, cultural performances, and fireworks.
long_description: BAPS Houston celebrates Diwali with a grand mela featuring the traditional lighting of diyas, rangoli competition, cultural performances by youth and adults, and a spectacular fireworks display. The community dinner serves traditional Gujarati and Indian festive sweets. A cherished annual tradition for Houston's Indian community.
venue_info: BAPS Mandir, Houston. Large parking lot. Family-friendly. Modest dress code inside the mandir.

title: Diwali Mela — Sunnyvale Hindu Temple
description: Annual Diwali Mela at Sunnyvale Hindu Temple with Lakshmi Puja, fireworks, and cultural performances.
long_description: Sunnyvale Hindu Temple's annual Diwali celebration features a grand Lakshmi Puja, cultural performances by community members, live music, and a spectacular fireworks display. Festive food stalls offer traditional sweets and savories. One of the Bay Area's most well-attended Diwali celebrations.
venue_info: 450 Persian Drive, Sunnyvale. Free parking. Expect heavy crowds — arrive early for best parking. Dress in festive attire.

title: Diwali Celebrations — Bharatiya Temple, Troy MI
description: Grand Diwali at Michigan's premier Hindu temple with Lakshmi Puja, cultural programs, and fireworks.
long_description: Bharatiya Temple's Diwali celebration is the highlight of the Detroit-area Hindu community's calendar. The day features special Lakshmi Puja, cultural performances by temple youth, traditional food stalls, and an evening fireworks display. One of the largest Diwali gatherings in the Midwest.
venue_info: 6850 Adams Rd, Troy, MI 48098. All-day event with parking on-site. Festival food vendors. Dress festively!

title: Diwali Festival — Hindu Temple of Arizona
description: Phoenix area Diwali celebration at the Hindu Temple of Arizona with traditional pujas and cultural programs.
long_description: The Hindu Temple of Arizona hosts the Phoenix metro's primary Diwali celebration. The program includes Lakshmi Puja, Ganesh Puja, cultural performances, children's activities, and festive food. The desert setting provides a unique backdrop for the thousands of diyas that illuminate the temple grounds.
venue_info: 3033 N Hayden Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85251. Free parking. Open 10 AM–9 PM on Diwali. Prasadam and festival food available.

title: Diwali Festival — Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago
description: Diwali celebrations at one of the largest Hindu temples in the Midwest with puja, fireworks, and cultural show.
long_description: The Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago in Lemont hosts its annual Diwali celebration, one of the Midwest's biggest. The evening features Lakshmi Puja, a grand cultural program, community dinner, and fireworks. The temple's stunning Rajasthani architecture creates a magical setting for the Festival of Lights.
venue_info: 10915 Lemont Rd, Lemont, IL. Large parking lot. Located about 30 miles southwest of downtown Chicago.

title: Diwali Celebrations — Sri Siva Vishnu Temple, Lanham MD
description: Grand Diwali festival at the DC area's premier Hindu temple with Lakshmi Puja, cultural performances, and fireworks.
organizer: Sri Siva Vishnu Temple Board of Trustees
long_description: The Sri Siva Vishnu Temple Diwali celebration draws thousands from across the DC/MD/VA region. The all-day program includes special Lakshmi Puja, Ganesh Puja, cultural performances, children's programs, and a spectacular fireworks display. The temple grounds are illuminated with diyas and festive decorations.
venue_info: 6905 Cipriano Rd, Lanham, MD 20706. All-day event. Shuttle service from overflow parking. Traditional dress encouraged.

title: UW Medicine Seattle Marathon and Half Marathon 2026
description: Seattle's flagship fall marathon with a scenic course through the city's most iconic neighborhoods. Half marathon and marathon options.
long_description: The UW Medicine Seattle Marathon is the city's premier fall distance race, offering full marathon and half marathon options. The course showcases Seattle's best — waterfront views, historic neighborhoods, and the iconic skyline. A Boston Marathon qualifier, the race attracts runners from across the Pacific Northwest. The November timing means cool temperatures ideal for distance running, though rain is always a possibility in Seattle.
venue_info: Memorial Stadium, 401 5th Ave N, Seattle Center. The course is a mix of flat waterfront stretches and moderate hills typical of Seattle. Light Rail and bus service reach Seattle Center. Packet pickup at the pre-race expo.

title: BMW Dallas Marathon 2026
description: Dallas's premier marathon weekend with full marathon, half, ultra, 5K, and relay options. Benefits Scottish Rite for Children.
long_description: The BMW Dallas Marathon has been a Texas running tradition for over 40 years. The race weekend features a full marathon, half marathon, ultra marathon, 5-person relay, 10K, and 5K — something for every runner. The course starts at Dallas City Hall, loops through scenic White Rock Lake, and finishes back downtown. Since 1997, the marathon has donated nearly $5 million to Scottish Rite for Children. The December timing provides cool running weather, and the event has sold out three consecutive years.
venue_info: Start/finish at Dallas City Hall, 1500 Marilla St. The course is flat and fast, passing through downtown Dallas and around White Rock Lake (120m total elevation gain). DART light rail serves the City Hall area. Post-race party with food, beer, and live music.
